caption:
Every quadratic question on the SAT wants one of four things: the zeros, the maximum, the minimum, or where the curve meets a line. Desmos hands you all four if you know where to click.

Save this for test week. Seva's practice tests have the same calculator built in, so you can drill the clicks until they're automatic. Free trial, link in bio.

#SAT #SATprep #SATmath #desmos #augustSAT #digitalSAT #sattips #testprep

slides.title: Type it in standard form, then click the curve
slides.caption: Type the equation and Desmos drops grey dots on both roots. Click one and the label appears: the solutions are $x = 2$ and $x = 4$.
slides.question: What are the solutions to $x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0$?

slides.title: The peak is already a point
slides.caption: Click the peak. The label $(2, 11)$ says the maximum value is $11$, and it happens at $x = 2$.
slides.question: What is the maximum value of $y = -2x^2 + 8x + 3$?

slides.title: The vertex sits halfway between the zeros
slides.caption: Halfway between the zeros $3$ and $-7$ is $x = -2$. Click the low point there: the minimum is $-25$.
slides.question: What is the minimum value of $y = (x - 3)(x + 7)$?

slides.title: A quadratic and a line cross twice
slides.caption: Type both equations exactly as written, then click each crossing. The solutions are $(1, 5)$ and $(4, 8)$.
slides.question: At which points do the graphs of $y = -x^2 + 6x$ and $y = x + 4$ intersect?

slides.title: Seva's practice tests have this exact calculator built in.
slides.body: Practice the clicks now so they're automatic when it counts.
